items.difficultyReason: Read and compare two distributions in a back-to-back plot, combine both sides to identify a mode, extract a class frequency and calculate its midpoint product, then explain why replacing individual values with class centres estimates the mean. These are linked, taught procedures with the required representations and comparison explicitly supplied.
items.independentDerivation: Female ages: 19, 27, 35, 42, 45, 50, 52, 53, 61, 62, 64, 64; male ages: 11, 12, 13, 20, 22, 22, 22, 24, 25, 30, 30, 31, 37, 46, 47, 52, 64, 64. Females are generally older (medians 51 and 27.5 years respectively), with a longer lower-age tail; males have a longer higher-age tail. Combined, 64 occurs four times and 22 three times, so 64 is the sole mode. The 30–39 values 35, 30, 30, 31, 37 give frequency 5; centre (30+39)/2 = 34.5 and product 172.5. The exact sum is 1146 for 30 students, mean 38.2. The six class frequencies are 4, 7, 5, 4, 4, 6 and midpoint products sum to 1185, giving 39.5. Grouping replaces exact values by class centres, explaining the difference.
